Welcome to Little Chalfont Primary School
Thank you for visiting our school website. We are a vibrant and nurturing primary school committed to providing a happy, safe and stimulating environment where every child can thrive. Our dedicated staff inspire a love of learning through a rich and exciting curriculum, encouraging curiosity, creativity and resilience from their very first steps with us. We firmly believe in the importance of partnership between home and school, working together to ensure all our pupils develop the essential skills, confidence and positive values needed to become ready, respectful and resillient individuals.
Our broad curriculum pages and year group overviews can be viewed through our curriculum tab.

At Little Chalfont Primary School (LCPS) we offer full wrap-around care from 7.30am to 6.00pm. Please see below for details of our breakfast club and after-school wrap-around care (WAC) provision.
Breakfast Club
Our breakfast club is co-ordinated and operated via LCPS staff.
Breakfast club runs from 7:30am to 8:30am for children in years 1 – 6 and from 7:30am to 9:00am for children in years Nursery and Reception.
Children are provided with a breakfast meal (cereal, milk and toast as chosen).
The charges per session for breakfast club are currently (2025-2026) as follows:
However, these charges will change to £10.00 per session for all year groups in the academic year 2026 – 2027, to fall in-line with the Chess Valley Primary Learning Trust charges.
To attend breakfast club, registration is essential as spaces are limited to ensure the safety of all children in our care. If you would like to apply for a space, please download and complete the registration form at the bottom of this page, and return it to the office. Once we have received your completed form, we will contact you to confirm whether a place is available for your child. If there is no place available, we will put your child on a waiting list.
Please note: Nursery places are strictly offered at the discretion of the school staff, on a case-by-case basis, depending on the individual child’s readiness to attend extended hours of care.
After-School Wrap-Around Care
At LCPS we have partnered with Premier Education to provide after-school wrap-around care. Premier Education are Ofsted registered and offer a range of stimulating activities in a safe, secure and fun environment, aiming to provide an outstanding service for busy parents.
Staff will adapt each day’s activities to the children’s needs or the weather. However, the timings and structure of each day remains consistent. Activities will be designed to fit with the school's termly themes and can include arts and crafts, baking, sports, Lego, games, quiet reading and general free play.
A healthy snack will be provided for all children who are staying until 6pm. Other children are welcome to bring their own fruit snack to eat. Please remember that LCPS is a nut and sesame-free school.
4.15pm – 6:00pm £8.00
3:15pm – 6:00pm £14.00
Booking your child's place:
All bookings must be made online, and you can do so by following the link here: Premier Education Wrap-around Care Bookings
When you book online, you can opt to pay with a card or childcare vouchers. If you would like to pay with childcare vouchers (CCV), you will need to add your preferred providers to your child's profile, which can be found in 'My Family'. As soon as this has been updated, you will be able to choose your provider under payment method. If you cannot see your provider listed, please contact us on the email address at the bottom of this email. You can view our list of registered childcare voucher providers here: Registered Childcare Voucher Providers
Collection procedure:
Collection between 3:15pm – 4:30pm: please buzz the school office at the gate, and you will be allowed access to the site as normal.
Collection after 4:30pm: the gate will be open for you to push (our contact number will be displayed at the gate if you need to contact us). Once you reach the main entrance door, ring the bell or call the team to notify a member of our team you are at the door.
We are grateful for your patience during the collection process as staff will be occupied delivering activities or preparing food for the afternoon snack, as well as retrieving your child for collection.
What's on each week at wrap-around care?
You can view the planned activities schedule for the forthcoming week on the Premier Education WAC timetable at the bottom of this page. If children do not want to take part in the main activity offered, they will have the opportunity to take part in other Premier Education-led sports clubs, games and general free play, depending on availability.
Premier Education Sports Clubs
Premier Education also offer a variety of after-school sports activities; booking can be accessed here: Premier Education After School Sports Club Bookings. Flyers for all Premier Education clubs can also be found under the extracurricular clubs tab of the LCPS website.
Don't forget that Premier Education sports clubs are available throughout the half-term as well. You can book online (pending availability) at any time.
Spaces are limited, therefore, if your child hasn't already booked a place for these sessions, we encourage you to do so soon.
If you have any questions or need further information, please reach out to our dedicated team:

If your question is still unanswered after reading our FAQs, please contact us on the relevant email address below:

French
Languages are an essential part of a broad, balanced curriculum. Not only do they provide an opportunity to communicate more effectively with others, they also help children to understand what it is to be a global citizen. This includes the importance of tolerance and understanding, which is crucial knowledge in today’s world.
Primary schools have had a legal responsibility to teach languages since 2014. The first cohort of pupils that studied languages throughout key stage 2 moved to secondary school in September 2018. At LCPS French is taught in Years 3-6, with an emphasis on fun, building confidence and exploring the patterns in language through songs, stories and games. There is also a French club for pupils in Year 2 providing a good foundation for foreign language teaching from Year 3 onwards.
We have specialist teaching in French and follow the Bucks Curriculum for Primary Modern Languages, which provides lots of resources for the Smartboard and worksheets for pupils as part of a scheme of work for KS2 French. We are also fortunate that the PTA pays our annual subscription to Linguascope, a website which pupils can use both in the classroom and at home. Our curriculum develops skills in speaking, reading, listening and writing, building on prior learning year on year and gradually developing accurate pronunciation and intonation. In their speaking work pupils are encouraged to engage in their own short conversations, express opinions and respond to others. In writing we work on accuracy, learning how to use a bilingual dictionary (the school has a class set) and understanding basic grammar, including masculine and feminine forms, conjugation of high frequency verbs and adjective agreement.
In the summer term we have a French café run by the Year 5 and 6 children to celebrate Bastille Day on 14th July and to raise cultural awareness of French traditions and customs. All students in Years 3-6 get a chance to order (and eat !) French food and drink.

Smartphone Free Childhood
This is a parent-led initiative at Little Chalfont Primary School that is supported by the school.
Supporting Our Children's Wellbeing Together
At Little Chalfont Primary School, we believe in fostering a childhood free from the pressures and risks associated with smartphones and social media.
In a powerful display of our school community coming together, so far over 130 parents have signed a Parent Pact pledging not to give their children smartphones before the age of 14 and to delay access to social media until 16.
This initiative, part of the national Smartphone Free Childhood movement, is designed to ensure children can grow, play, and develop without the negative effects of digital distractions.
Why Delay Smartphones and Social Media?
More and more scientific research is backing up parental experience to show that early smartphone and social media exposure can be harmful to children. Some of the biggest concerns include:
There are many great sources of information on the challenges that come from Smartphones and Social Media. Here are a few:
We have a longer list or resources on the subject available here.
A Community Effort to Reduce Social Pressure
One of the biggest challenges parents face is peer pressure – both for themselves and their children. Many parents feel forced to give their child a smartphone simply because “everyone else has one.” The Parent Pact at Little Chalfont Primary helps remove this pressure by creating a unified community approach.
Today, 94% of of primary school parents think smartphones are harmful. Yet, 90% of children have smartphones by year 7. This happens because the social pressure becomes unbearable once the majority of children have smartphones in a class.
The Parent Pact aims to break this cycle by enabling parents to socially coordinate and to have the confidence that their child won’t be socially excluded if they don’t have a smartphone.
Learn More – Watch Our Parents' Meeting
To help parents make informed decisions, we held a Parents' Meeting in January 2024. Below are resources from the event:
We’re not anti-tech, we’re pro-childhood
We recognise that technology has immense benefits, and young people should be able to enjoy the opportunities it creates – when they’re ready and when it’s safe to do so.
But childhood is precious and fleeting. All children should have the opportunity to learn, develop and grow free from the addictive-by-design algorithms and age-inappropriate content of social media and smartphones.
The Smartphone Free Childhood Movement recommends that if parents want to give their child a phone, that they give their child a simple phone instead of a smartphone until the end of Year 9 (at the earliest). That means you can keep in touch when they’re out and about using calls and texts, without any of the harms associated with smartphones and social media.
When children want to use the internet, we recommend that they do so on a shared family computer, which could even have WhatsApp on it if you feel comfortable with that. This way they can get acquainted with the digital world and stay connected to their friends without the temptation of having it in their pocket 24/7.
For a list of alternatives to smartphones, see here.
Why do I need to do this now? Can’t I wait?
We recognise that for parents and carers of children in younger years that this challenge may feel a long way off. However, it is far easier to engage with this topic before it becomes an issue. As children start to get smartphones in the later years of primary school, it is much, much harder to socially coordinate. We therefore encourage all new parents to sign this pact so that it is not something that you have to worry about during your time at Little Chalfont.
The 2024/5 Year One class are a great example of this. 80% of the children are enrolled in the Parent Pact.
What about when they go to secondary school?
Little Chalfont Primary is leading the way on this in the local area. This effort is part of a national initiative. The parents at Little Chalfont are looking to engage other local primary schools and secondary schools so that by the time our children go to secondary school, most new parents in the secondary school will have signed the pact in advance of the transition.
Join the Movement – Sign the Parent Pact
Since launching nationally in September 2023, over 165,000 parents have signed the Smartphone Free Childhood pact, including 1,700 parents in Buckinghamshire. Little Chalfont Primary is one of the leading schools in the county.
You can see the Buckinghamshire league table here.

We invite all parents at Little Chalfont Primary to join us in this commitment and help protect childhood from digital harm.
